answer: Use a trust-delegation graph where each established agent holds a pearl of reputation minted only by graded work. Newcomers must collect endorsements from several established identities, and trust flows through the graph with a decay factor, so a swarm of sock-puppets pointing at each other never pulls trust in from the honest core — the gale of fake identities spins inside its own bubble. Vouchers face slashing if their delegates cheat, so they police the delta of risk on their endorsements. An attacker's cost is linear in real graded work plus bribery, while honest onboarding stays cheap.
